Opaque handle to a provider that signals when buffers have been processed.

Opaque handle to an audio decoder that reads from a data stream and fills audio buffers.
Opaque generic encoder handle; query type to cast to blocking or streaming encoders.

Opaque handle to a streaming encoder that produces encoded chunks and can finalize to a URI.
Opaque handle to a high-level audio stream that provides buffers and controls playback position/duration.
Opaque handle to a standalone audio player instance operating on a URL and output with callbacks.
Opaque handle to a database connection used by library and queries.
Opaque handle to a prepared database statement for binding, stepping, and reading columns.

Callback interface struct for audio player lifecycle and events.
Callback interface struct for indexer progress and completion notifications.
Gain parameters for the audio player, including preamp, gain, and peak values.

Aggregate context struct bundling core services, DB connection, prefs, and internal state for a plugin or application instance.
Standard library string type included via <string>. It is referenced in this header but not defined here, so it should be ignored per instructions. No custom types are defined in this header.
Strongly-typed enumeration of high-level player states used by the SDK.
Strongly-typed enumeration describing the lifecycle/progress state of an audio stream instance.
Strongly-typed enumeration controlling repeat behavior of playback.
Strongly-typed enumeration for return/status values from audio output write/queue operations.
Strongly-typed enumeration indicating the type of position change request (seek vs. scrub).
Strongly-typed enumeration of well-known filesystem path categories used by the application/SDK.
Strongly-typed bitflag-like enumeration describing optional capabilities (currently only Prebuffer).
Unscoped enumeration indicating the result of a library scan transaction (commit or rollback).
Strongly-typed enumeration controlling how ReplayGain is applied (disabled, track-based, or album-based).
Strongly-typed enumeration selecting the transport behavior between tracks (gapless or crossfade).
Unscoped enumeration of flags used when opening resources (bitwise combinable values).
Strongly-typed enumeration of stream options/flags (e.g., disable DSP).
Strongly-typed enumeration representing the loading state of track or resource metadata.

Abstract interface for memory allocation across plugin and host boundaries. Provides Allocate and Free so the host can allocate/free memory on behalf of a plugin using the plugin’s allocator. Concrete implementations must ensure symmetry between Allocate and Free. No ownership or thread-safety guarantees are specified in this header.

Pure virtual interface for an audio analysis component that processes buffers and writes results to an ITagStore. Implementations are responsible for lifetime via Release() and for a Start/Analyze/End lifecycle. Details like threading, ownership, and error handling are not specified in this header.

Abstract interface for a blocking audio encoder that writes encoded output to an IDataStream. Implementations must be able to initialize with sample rate, channel count, and target bitrate, accept PCM input via IBuffer in Encode, and perform any required flushing/teardown in Finalize. It derives from IEncoder, so it follows the broader encoder contract while enforcing synchronous/blocking operation. Details about threading, lifetime, and error semantics beyond return values are not specified here.

Abstract interface for an audio buffer in musik::core::sdk. Exposes sample rate, channel count, number of samples, total byte size, and a pointer to the underlying float sample data. Implementations must manage lifetime via the Release() method (no virtual destructor is provided), implying custom reference counting or factory ownership semantics. BufferPointer() returns a pointer to interleaved float samples if channels > 1; exact layout is not specified here.

Abstract interface for components that provide or manage audio/data buffers and need notification when a buffer has finished processing. It declares a single pure-virtual callback OnBufferProcessed that receives a pointer to an IBuffer. No destructor is declared; lifetime management details are not specified in this header.

Forward-referenced interface representing a buffer, included via IBuffer.h. This header only references it; the actual definition resides elsewhere. Used as a parameter to IBufferProvider::OnBufferProcessed.

Abstract interface for a digital signal processing (DSP) unit that operates on audio buffers. Implementations must provide Process to transform the provided IBuffer and Release for lifetime management (custom deletion). Details of IBuffer come from IBuffer.h and are not defined here.

objects.definition: typedef long PositionType;
objects.description: Alias for long used to represent stream positions, sizes, and byte counts within the SDK.

Abstract interface for readable/writable byte streams in the musik::core::sdk. Implementers provide backing I/O (e.g., files, network). Lifecycle is managed via virtual Release(); users should call Close() when done. Positioning uses PositionType and supports querying length, EOF, and seekability. Thread interruption supported via Interrupt(). Type() returns a stream type identifier; Uri() returns the source URI.

Abstract factory interface for creating IDataStream instances from a URI. Provides capability probing via CanRead, construction via Open with specified OpenFlags, and lifecycle management via Release. The OpenFlags alias refers to musik::core::sdk::OpenFlags defined elsewhere. Implementation details, ownership semantics of returned IDataStream*, and exact meaning of flags are not documented in this header.

Pure virtual interface for emitting debug/log messages at various severity levels (Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). Implementations should route messages to the host application's logging system. The two parameters are a short tag/category and the message text. Lifetime, ownership, and threading guarantees are not specified in this header.

Abstract interface for an audio decoder responsible for opening a data stream, decoding audio into an IBuffer, seeking, reporting duration, and signaling exhaustion. Implementations must manage their own lifetime via Release(). Other referenced types (IBuffer, IDataStream) are declared in included headers and not defined here.

Abstract factory interface for creating IDecoder instances within the musik::core::sdk namespace. It exposes a method to construct a decoder, query if the factory can handle a specific type (likely a codec or MIME/extension string), and a Release method for lifetime management. Details about ownership and destruction are not provided here; typically Release deletes the factory when called on implementations.

Referenced decoder interface type returned by IDecoderFactory::CreateDecoder(). It is not defined in this header; it is forward-declared via the included IDecoder.h. No further details available here.

Abstract interface representing a device with an identifier and a displayable name. Lifetime is managed via Release(); implementers should provide reference-counted or corresponding destruction in Release().
Abstract interface representing a collection of IDevice instances. Provides count and indexed access. Caller must call Release() when finished with the list if the provider requires it.

Abstract interface representing an encoder component in the musik::core::sdk namespace. It exposes a single method, Release(), for freeing the instance. No other behavior is specified here; actual encoding APIs are likely defined elsewhere. Being an interface, it is expected to be implemented by concrete encoder classes and managed via Release() rather than delete.

Abstract factory interface for creating IEncoder instances based on an input type string and for querying support for a given type. Implementations must provide lifetime management via Release(). Details about IEncoder are referenced but defined elsewhere.

Abstract interface providing access to the musikcube runtime environment for plugins or components. It exposes factory/accessor methods for streams, codecs, buffers, preferences, debugging, outputs, replay gain, EQ, transport type, and metadata indexing. As a pure virtual class, it must be implemented by the host; lifetime, construction, and ownership semantics are defined by the host API and are not specified in this header.

Abstract interface declaring a notifier capable of scheduling a rescan for a given indexer source. It exposes a single pure-virtual method ScheduleRescan that accepts a pointer to an IIndexerSource. The class is intended to be implemented by components that trigger or request index rescans within the indexing subsystem. No destructor is declared here; implementers should provide a virtual destructor to avoid potential leaks when deleting via base pointer.

Abstract interface for an indexer source used by musik::core::sdk. Implementations supply media items to the indexer and optionally scan individual tracks. Provides lifecycle hooks (OnBeforeScan/OnAfterScan), full and per-track scanning, interruption, and metadata about ID stability and a source identifier. Release indicates manual lifetime management via the interface. Other referenced types (ScanResult, IIndexerWriter, ITagStore) are declared in included headers and are not defined here.

objects.definition: class IIndexerSource;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an indexer source interface used by IIndexerWriter methods. Only declared here; no definition provided in this header, so its members and lifecycle are unknown.

Abstract interface for writing index data to a tag store for a specific IIndexerSource. Provides operations to create a writable tag store, save/update track metadata, commit progress, remove items by URI or external ID, bulk-remove all items for a source, and query last-modified timestamps. The concrete implementation, ownership rules, and destruction semantics are not specified here.

Abstract key/value lookup interface derived from IValue. Provides typed accessors to retrieve values by string key as string, int64, int32, or double. Implementations are expected to store and return values; this header only declares the interface and does not define storage semantics. Ownership, lifetime, and construction are unspecified here.

Interface representing a list of IMap objects in the musik::core::sdk namespace. It exposes reference/lifetime management via Release(), random access via GetAt(), and size via Count(). Concrete implementations are expected to manage a sequence of IMap pointers. Details such as ownership semantics of returned IMap* and the calling convention for Release() are not documented here and are therefore unknown.

Abstract interface for querying and manipulating metadata in the musikcube core: tracks, categories, albums, and playlists, and for issuing raw metadata queries. Implementations are expected to manage returned object lifetimes via their own Release semantics; this header does not specify ownership beyond virtual methods. Details of memory management for returned pointers (e.g., whether caller must Release) are not documented here.

Pure virtual interface for an audio output backend in the musikcube SDK. Implementations manage playback (play/pause/stop), volume, device selection, latency, and buffer consumption from an IBufferProvider. Lifetime is managed via Release(); construction details are not provided here. OutputState, IBuffer, IBufferProvider, IDeviceList, and IDevice are referenced but defined elsewhere.

Abstract interface for a PCM visualizer within the musik core SDK. Inherits from IVisualizer (declared elsewhere). Provides a method to write visualization data derived from PCM audio into a target IBuffer, and a Release method for lifetime management. Exact ownership and threading semantics are not specified in this header.

Abstract interface for a playback remote/controller in musik::core::sdk. Consumers implement this to receive playback-related events (track change, state/time/volume/mode/queue changes) and to be given an IPlaybackService to control playback. Lifetime is managed by implementer; Release() suggests reference-counted or manual lifetime protocol but specifics are not defined here.

Abstract interface for controlling playback within the musik::core::sdk. Provides operations to start/stop playback, navigate tracks, query and set repeat/shuffle, playback state, volume, time position, mute, and playlist management. Also exposes methods to edit and clone the current playlist, and to reload the output device. All methods are pure-virtual; lifetime and construction are owned by the hosting application or factory outside this header.

Abstract interface for a musikcube plugin. Implementers provide metadata (name, version, author, GUID), lifecycle hooks (Release, Reload), optional configuration support, and the SDK version they target. This is a pure-virtual class; instances are created by plugin implementations outside this header. Ownership and destruction are managed via the Release() method (caller should invoke Release when done). Details beyond this interface are not specified here.

Abstract interface for a key/value preferences store within musik::core::sdk. Provides typed getters and setters for bool, int, double, and string values, a Save() method to persist changes, and Release() for lifetime management when used across ABI boundaries. Strings are retrieved via GetString using a caller-supplied buffer; a preliminary call with dst == nullptr and size == 0 returns the required byte count (including terminator). Ownership and destruction are handled by the implementer; clients must call Release() when finished if the object is ref-counted or otherwise managed by the provider. Specific storage backend and persistence semantics are not defined here.

Abstract interface representing a resource within the musikcore SDK. It provides a unique identifier, a classification (Value or Map), a type string, and a manual lifetime management hook via Release(). Implementations are expected to be reference-counted or otherwise managed and must override the pure virtual methods.
Strongly-typed enum nested in IResource that classifies a resource as either a scalar Value or an associative Map. Used as the return type of IResource::GetClass().

Abstract interface describing a schema of configuration entries used by the musik::core::sdk. Provides enumeration of entries and defines nested types for entry metadata and value constraints across several kinds (bool, int, double, string, enum). Implementations own and manage Entry instances and support Release/Count/At for lifetime and access.
Strongly-typed enumeration of the kinds of schema entries supported by ISchema: boolean, integer, double, string, and enum.
Base record for a schema entry containing its Type and name. Specialized entry structs embed this as their first field.
Schema entry for a boolean value. Stores common Entry metadata and a default value.
Schema entry for an integer value with inclusive min/max bounds and a default.
Schema entry for a double-precision value with bounds, display/rounding precision, and a default.
Schema entry for a string value, holding default string (C-string).
Schema entry representing an enumeration of string choices. Contains a list of possible values and a default value.

Concrete, heap-managed schema builder implementing ISchema. Owns dynamically allocated Entry records and associated strings. Provides fluent Add* methods to construct the schema and cleans up all allocated memory in the destructor. Release deletes this. Count/At expose stored entries. Allocation helpers manage C-strings and arrays for enum values.

Abstract interface for a spectrum visualizer within the musik::core::sdk API. Implementations receive spectrum magnitude data via Write() and are expected to display or process it. Release() is the interface-level destructor counterpart for manual lifetime management. Inherits from IVisualizer (not defined in this header).

Abstract interface for a streaming audio encoder used to encode PCM buffers into a compressed stream suitable for writing to a destination identified by a URI. It derives from IEncoder (declared elsewhere). Implementations must provide lifecycle: Initialize with sample rate, channel count, and target bitrate; Encode PCM input (IBuffer) and return encoded bytes via an output data buffer; Flush remaining encoder state producing any final bytes; and Finalize to commit/close the stream for the specified URI. Memory ownership and allocation strategy for the returned data buffers are not specified in this header and must be defined by the concrete implementation or accompanying API docs.

Abstract interface for tag readers in the musikcore SDK. Implementations parse metadata from a media resource identified by a URI and write it into an ITagStore. Provides capability querying via CanRead for file extensions and manual lifetime control via Release. Destruction semantics are not explicitly documented; Release implies custom allocator/ownership patterns.

Abstract interface for a reference-counted tag store within musik::core::sdk. It allows setting, clearing, and querying string key/value metadata tags, setting an optional thumbnail image as raw bytes, checking thumbnail presence, and applying ReplayGain metadata. Ownership is managed via Retain/Release; implementers must provide reference counting. The ReplayGain type is referenced from ReplayGain.h and not defined here.

Abstract interface representing a track object in the musikcore SDK. It derives from IMap (a key/value metadata interface, declared elsewhere). Provides reference management via Retain(), a method to fetch the track URI into a caller-provided buffer, and accessors for replay gain and metadata state. Concrete implementations are provided outside this header.

Abstract interface representing a list/collection of tracks. Provides methods to query the number of tracks, obtain a track ID by index, find an index by track ID, retrieve a track object by index, and release the list. Implementations are responsible for lifetime management via Release, suggesting reference-counted or manual destruction semantics. The ITrack type is referenced but defined elsewhere.

Forward-referenced track interface type used by ITrackList::GetTrack. Its definition is not present in this header; it is included via "ITrack.h". Details about its members and lifecycle are unknown here.

Pure virtual interface for editing a track list in the musik::core::sdk namespace. Provides operations to insert, swap, move, delete, add, clear, and shuffle track items identified by 64-bit IDs, plus a Release() method for manual lifetime management. Implementation details (ownership semantics, error handling) are not provided in this header; Release() implies reference-counted or manual deletion via the interface.

Abstract interface representing a resource that can provide a value as a character buffer. Inherits from IResource (defined elsewhere). Implementations must supply GetValue to copy a value into the caller-provided buffer and return the number of bytes written or required. Exact semantics beyond this are not documented here.

Abstract interface representing a list of IValue items in the musik::core::sdk namespace. It exposes reference-lifecycle management via Release(), a Count() method to obtain the number of elements, and GetAt(index) to access elements by position. Actual storage and ownership semantics are defined by implementers; the presence of Release() suggests manual lifetime management (reference counting or custom deletion) rather than standard delete.

Abstract interface for a visualizer plugin within the musikcube SDK. Implementations are expected to manage their own lifetime (Release), control UI visibility (Show/Hide/Visible), and provide a human-readable name (Name). The header provides no ownership or threading guarantees; construction occurs outside this header, likely via plugin factory mechanisms declared elsewhere. Details such as required destruction semantics beyond Release and whether methods are thread-safe are not specified.

Struct holding ReplayGain metadata values for audio: per-track gain and peak, and per-album gain and peak, all as floats. Used to normalize playback loudness. No constructors or special ownership semantics are defined here.

functions.name: mcsdk_env_init
functions.description: Initializes global musikcube SDK environment/state. Call before using other SDK APIs that depend on global environment.
requirements: Must be called before environment-dependent APIs (unknown exact set).
Safe to call once at process startup; repeated calls behavior unknown.

functions.name: mcsdk_env_release
functions.description: Releases/shuts down the global musikcube SDK environment and associated resources.
requirements: Should be called after mcsdk_env_init when the SDK is no longer needed.
Do not call other environment-dependent APIs after release.
Call exactly once at shutdown; behavior of multiple calls is unknown.

functions.name: mcsdk_context_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new instance context containing service handles (metadata, playback, indexer, library, db, preferences, internal).
requirements: context must be a valid, non-null pointer to a mcsdk_context* (output).
The function assigns/allocates the context; caller must later release with mcsdk_context_release.

functions.name: mcsdk_context_release
functions.description: Releases and destroys a previously initialized instance context and its contained handles.
requirements: context must be a valid, non-null pointer to a mcsdk_context* that was obtained from mcsdk_context_init.
After return, the stored pointer may be invalidated/cleared; do not reuse.

functions.name: mcsdk_set_plugin_context
functions.description: Sets the current thread/module's plugin context, enabling plugin APIs to reference a specific instance context.
requirements: context must point to a valid mcsdk_context.
Must be called in plugin code paths that require a bound context. Exact lifetime/threading semantics unknown.

functions.name: mcsdk_is_plugin_context
functions.description: Returns whether the given context is the active plugin context.
requirements: context must point to a valid mcsdk_context or be null (behavior with null unknown).

functions.name: mcsdk_resource_get_id
functions.description: Retrieves the unique identifier of a resource.
requirements: r must be a valid resource handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_resource_get_class
functions.description: Returns the class/type of the resource (value or map).
requirements: r must be a valid resource handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_resource_release
functions.description: Releases a resource handle and its underlying object.
requirements: r must be a valid resource handle obtained from the SDK.
Do not use r after release.

functions.name: mcsdk_value_get_value
functions.signature: size_t mcsdk_value_get_value(mcsdk_value v, char* dst, size_t size)
functions.description: Copies the string representation of a value into dst. Returns number of bytes written or required.
requirements: v must be a valid value handle.
dst may be NULL to query required size; if non-null, it must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size should include space for the terminating NUL if a C-string is expected (unspecified).

functions.name: mcsdk_value_release
functions.description: Releases a value handle.
requirements: v must be a valid value handle.
Do not use v after release.

functions.name: mcsdk_value_list_count
functions.description: Returns the number of entries in a value list.
requirements: vl must be a valid value list handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_value_list_get_at
functions.description: Retrieves the value at the specified index.
requirements: vl must be a valid value list handle.
index must be less than mcsdk_value_list_count(vl).
Returned mcsdk_value must be released with mcsdk_value_release when no longer needed (typical handle pattern; exact ownership unknown).

functions.name: mcsdk_value_list_release
functions.description: Releases a value list handle and its resources.
requirements: vl must be a valid value list handle.
Do not access vl after release.

functions.name: mcsdk_map_get_string
functions.signature: int mcsdk_map_get_string(mcsdk_map m, const char* key, char* dst, int size)
functions.description: Looks up a string field in a map by key and copies it into dst. Returns number of bytes written or required.
requirements: m must be a valid map handle.
key must be a non-null, null-terminated string.
dst may be NULL to query required size; if non-null, must have at least size bytes.
size should include space for terminating NUL if a C-string is expected (unspecified).

functions.name: mcsdk_map_get_int64
functions.signature: int64_t mcsdk_map_get_int64(mcsdk_map m, const char* key, int64_t default_value)
functions.description: Gets a 64-bit integer field from the map by key, or returns default_value if not present.
requirements: m must be a valid map handle.
key must be a non-null, null-terminated string.

functions.name: mcsdk_map_get_int32
functions.signature: int32_t mcsdk_map_get_int32(mcsdk_map m, const char* key, int32_t default_value)
functions.description: Gets a 32-bit integer field from the map by key, or returns default_value if not present.
requirements: m must be a valid map handle.
key must be a non-null, null-terminated string.

functions.name: mcsdk_map_get_double
functions.signature: double mcsdk_map_get_double(mcsdk_map m, const char* key, double default_value)
functions.description: Gets a floating-point field from the map by key, or returns default_value if not present.
requirements: m must be a valid map handle.
key must be a non-null, null-terminated string.

functions.name: mcsdk_map_release
functions.description: Releases a map handle.
requirements: m must be a valid map handle.
Do not use m after release.

functions.name: mcsdk_map_list_get_count
functions.description: Returns the number of maps in a map list.
requirements: ml must be a valid map list handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_map_list_get_at
functions.description: Retrieves the map at the specified index.
requirements: ml must be a valid map list handle.
index must be less than mcsdk_map_list_get_count(ml).
Returned map handle must be released with mcsdk_map_release when no longer needed (ownership semantics not explicitly stated).

functions.name: mcsdk_map_list_release
functions.description: Releases a map list handle.
requirements: ml must be a valid map list handle.
Do not use ml after release.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_retain
functions.description: Increments the retain/reference count for a track handle.
requirements: t must be a valid track handle.
Use mcsdk_track_release to decrement when done.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_get_uri
functions.signature: int mcsdk_track_get_uri(mcsdk_track t, char* dst, int size)
functions.description: Copies the track's URI into dst. Returns bytes written or required.
requirements: t must be a valid track handle.
dst may be NULL to query required size; if non-null, it must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size should include space for NUL terminator (unspecified).

functions.name: mcsdk_track_release
functions.description: Decrements the retain/reference count or releases a track handle.
requirements: t must be a valid track handle.
Do not use t after final release.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_get_count
functions.description: Returns the number of tracks in the list.
requirements: tl must be a valid track list handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_get_id
functions.description: Retrieves the track id at the specified index within the list.
requirements: tl must be a valid track list handle.
index must be less than mcsdk_track_list_get_count(tl).

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_index_of
functions.description: Returns the index of the given track id in the list, or a sentinel if not found (exact not specified).
requirements: tl must be a valid track list handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_get_track_at
functions.description: Returns the track handle at the specified index.
requirements: tl must be a valid track list handle.
index must be less than mcsdk_track_list_get_count(tl).
Caller is responsible for releasing the returned track with mcsdk_track_release (ownership not explicitly stated).

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_release
functions.description: Releases a track list handle and its resources.
requirements: tl must be a valid track list handle.
Do not use tl after release.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_create
functions.description: Creates a new (editable) track list associated with the provided context.
requirements: context must point to a valid initialized mcsdk_context.
Caller must release the returned handle with mcsdk_track_list_release.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_can_edit
functions.description: Returns whether the specified track list supports editing.
requirements: tl must be a valid track list handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_edit
functions.description: Returns an editor handle to mutate the track list.
requirements: tl must be a valid track list handle that is editable.
Caller must release the editor with mcsdk_track_list_editor_release.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_editor_insert
functions.signature: bool mcsdk_track_list_editor_insert(mcsdk_track_list_editor tle, int64_t id, size_t index)
functions.description: Inserts a track id into the list at index.
requirements: tle must be a valid track list editor handle.
index must be within valid insertion range [0..count].
id must refer to a valid track in the library (semantics not enforced here).

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_editor_swap
functions.signature: bool mcsdk_track_list_editor_swap(mcsdk_track_list_editor tle, size_t index1, size_t index2)
functions.description: Swaps two items in the track list.
requirements: tle must be a valid track list editor handle.
index1 and index2 must both be valid indices in the list.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_editor_move
functions.signature: bool mcsdk_track_list_editor_move(mcsdk_track_list_editor tle, size_t from, size_t to)
functions.description: Moves an item from one index to another.
requirements: tle must be a valid track list editor handle.
from and to must be within the list range.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_editor_delete
functions.description: Deletes the item at the specified index from the track list.
requirements: tle must be a valid track list editor handle.
index must be a valid list index.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_editor_add
functions.description: Appends a track id to the end of the track list.
requirements: tle must be a valid track list editor handle.

functions.name: mcsdk_track_list_editor_clear

functions.name: DataBuffer::DataBuffer
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes an empty buffer with data == nullptr and offset == rawLength == length == 0. Use before any other member function to ensure the buffer starts in a known state.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object is initially empty; no allocations are performed until reset(), append(), pad(), or from() are called.
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if used across threads.

functions.name: DataBuffer::~DataBuffer
functions.description: Destructor. Releases any heap-allocated storage owned by the buffer via delete[]. After destruction, any pointers previously returned (e.g., via pos() or data) become invalid.
requirements: All outstanding pointers into the buffer (e.g., from pos() or data) must not be dereferenced after destruction.
Do not double-delete; object must not be destroyed twice.
Not thread-safe; ensure no concurrent access during destruction.

functions.name: DataBuffer::reset
functions.description: Resets the buffer to the specified logical length, allocating or growing capacity if needed. If newLength exceeds current rawLength, a new T[newLength] is allocated and old data is discarded. Sets length = newLength and offset = 0.
requirements: newLength is the desired element count in units of T (inferred from allocation with new T[newLength]).
Existing data content is not preserved when a reallocation occurs; caller must not expect previous contents to remain.
After call, valid data range is [0, length). Content is uninitialized; caller should fill it before reading.
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.

functions.name: DataBuffer::zero
functions.description: Logically clears the buffer (offset = 0, length = 0) and fills the entire allocated region (rawLength elements) with zero bytes using memset. Useful for scrubbing or initializing capacity to zeros.
requirements: T must be trivially byte-addressable for memset to be meaningful; otherwise semantic zeroing may not create valid T objects (inferred).
If data is nullptr, no action is taken.
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.

functions.name: DataBuffer::from
functions.signature: template<typename T> void DataBuffer<T>::from(T* source, size_t size)
functions.description: Replaces the buffer contents by copying from source. Allocates/resizes to size elements via reset(size), then copies size bytes from source into data using memcpy, and sets length = size. Note: uses raw byte count in memcpy, which is inconsistent with T-sized element semantics; intended primarily for byte-sized T (e.g., uint8_t/char).
requirements: source must point to a readable memory region of at least size bytes.
If size > 0, source must be non-null.
For non-byte-sized T, behavior is ambiguous because memcpy copies size bytes but allocation was for size T elements; use only when T is 1 byte (inferred).
After call, length equals size (not size in elements), so for non-byte types this may represent bytes rather than element count (inferred).
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.

functions.name: DataBuffer::realloc
functions.description: Ensures there is sufficient capacity to append size more elements (in units of T). If length + size > rawLength, grows capacity to (length + size) * 2, allocates new storage, and preserves existing content via memcpy of length * sizeof(T).
requirements: size is a count of additional T elements intended to be appended.
Existing data is preserved when growing; callers should treat any pointers into the old buffer as invalid after a growth (data pointer may change).
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.

functions.name: DataBuffer::append
functions.signature: template<typename T> int DataBuffer<T>::append(const T* source, size_t size)
functions.description: Appends size elements from source to the end of the buffer. Ensures capacity via realloc(size), copies size * sizeof(T) bytes, updates length by size, and returns the number of elements appended as an int.
requirements: source must point to at least size contiguous T elements; if size > 0, source must be non-null.
size is a count of T elements (multiplied by sizeof(T) for the copy).
For overlapping ranges with this->data, behavior is undefined due to memcpy; ensure no overlap.
Return value is truncated to int if size exceeds INT_MAX (inferred).
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.

functions.name: DataBuffer::pad
functions.signature: template<typename T> int DataBuffer<T>::pad(char value, size_t size)
functions.description: Extends the buffer by size elements and fills the new region with the byte value using memset. Updates length by size and returns the number added. Intended for byte buffers; for larger T, this sets each byte of the new region to value, not logical T values.
requirements: size is a count of T elements to add.
For non-byte-sized T, memset will fill raw bytes, which may not produce meaningful T values (inferred).
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.
Return value is truncated to int if size exceeds INT_MAX (inferred).

functions.name: DataBuffer::empty

requirements: None beyond object being valid.

functions.name: DataBuffer::avail

requirements: Interpretation of the unit matches length/offset units used by other methods; typically counts of T elements except where from() ambiguity exists (inferred).

functions.name: DataBuffer::pos
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current position within the buffer: data + offset. Useful for reading/writing from the current offset.
requirements: If data is nullptr, returned pointer is undefined; ensure buffer has been allocated or length/offset set appropriately before dereferencing.
Pointer may be invalidated by any operation that reallocates (e.g., append/pad/realloc).

functions.name: DataBuffer::inc
functions.description: Advances the current offset by count elements. If the offset reaches or exceeds length, both offset and length are reset to 0 (logically empty).
requirements: count is in units of T elements, consistent with length/offset.

Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.

functions.name: DataBuffer::swap

requirements: with must be a DataBuffer instance with the same template parameter T.

Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if shared.

functions.signature:

void musik::core::sdk::fs::scanDirectory(const std::string& path, std::function<void(const std::string&)> callback, std::function<bool()> interrupt = std::function<bool()>())

Expected usage: pass a pointer obtained from this allocator’s Allocate back to Free when no longer needed. Notes: this implementation calls free(data); per the C standard, free(NULL) is a no-op.
requirements: Only pass pointers obtained from the same PluginAllocator<T>::Allocate.

Do not pass pointers allocated by a different allocator or by new/delete.
